value_stream.name: Corporate Social Responsibility, Foundation & Community Investment

fields.Participants: Strategy (VS-33), ESG (VS-25), Marketing (VS-14.3), Govt Affairs (VS-104), Board (VS-36)
fields.Trigger: Corporate strategy (VS-33); board review; community/stakeholder signal
fields.Volume: One enterprise CSR strategy across 200 store communities

Automation Opportunity: - Community-priority/stakeholder analytics; strategy-to-program linkage tracking; social-license dashboard
Controls: - CTL-686: CSR strategy board-endorsed (VS-36); aligned to corporate purpose (VS-33); community-priority-informed
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-25 (ESG), VS-36 (board), VS-14.3 (brand), VS-104 (govt affairs), W4508 (budget), W4514 (programs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Strategic-disconnect risk**: CSR detached from corporate purpose → wasted/low-impact spend; mitigated by strategy alignment & board endorsement
- **Social-license-blind risk**: Programs miss actual community priorities; mitigated by stakeholder mapping & community input
System Touchpoints: - Strategy/CPM (VS-33); ESG (VS-25); board governance (VS-36); marketing/brand (VS-14.3); govt affairs (VS-104)

steps.activity: Foundation ED/Sustainability Lead set the CSR strategy and pillars (e.g., shelter/housing, livelihood, education, disaster resilience, environment), aligned to BuildRight's "Home Building Partner" purpose and corporate strategy (VS-33)
Foundation ED/Stakeholders map social-license priorities per region/community (Mindanao HQ, Visayas, Luzon) using community/stakeholder input (links to VS-104/VS-44), and sequence the portfolio
Foundation ED/Sustainability Lead document the strategy, obtain board endorsement (VS-36), and cascade to program design (W4514), budget (W4508), and reporting (W4525)

fields.Trigger: Foundation formation; regulatory change; BIR re-accreditation
fields.Volume: One BuildRight Foundation legal entity + donee status

workflows.name: Foundation Legal Setup, SEC Registration & BIR Qualified-Donee Status

Automation Opportunity: - Regulatory-calendar tracker with renewal alerts; donor-receipt automation; accreditation document vault
Controls: - CTL-686: Foundation SEC-registered & purpose-bounded; BIR donee status maintained; PCNC accredited (W4507)
Cross-references: - links to VS-100.3 (legal), VS-79 (tax/BIR), VS-22 (compliance), VS-17 (finance), VS-36 (governance), W4507 (PCNC)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lapsed-accreditation risk**: BIR donee/PCNC status lapses → donations non-deductible, donor flight; mitigated by regulatory calendar & renewal SLA
- **Purpose-drift risk**: Foundation activity outside its legal purpose clause → regulatory exposure; mitigated by purpose-clause discipline

steps.activity: Legal/Foundation ED register the Foundation with SEC (Articles, Bylaws, purpose clause), secure LGU/permits, and establish the legal/operating framework distinct from operating entities (profile §2)
Tax/Legal secure and maintain BIR qualified-donee status (donations deductible, tax-deductible receipts) and the PCNC accreditation (W4507), with annual revalidation
Compliance/Legal maintain the regulatory calendar (SEC filings, BIR donee re-accreditation, PCNC renewal, LGU permits) and manage audit response (VS-22/VS-21)

fields.Trigger: Board cycle; PCNC cycle; governance review

Automation Opportunity: - Board/COI/governance management (VS-36); PCNC evidence-pack automation; fund-use dashboards
Controls: - CTL-686: Foundation board independent w/ COI policy; separately audited (VS-21); PCNC accredited
Cross-references: - links to VS-36 (governance), VS-21 (audit), VS-17 (finance), VS-100.3 (legal), W4506 (donee status)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Governance-weakness risk**: Weak board/oversight → misuse/perception of misuse; mitigated by independence, COI policy, separate audit
- **Credibility-loss risk**: PCNC lapse → partner/donor confidence loss; mitigated by accreditation maintenance
Time Estimate: - Board ~quarterly; PCNC ~per 3-year cycle with annual upkeep

steps.activity: Board/Corp Secretary run Foundation governance (board composition, independence, conflict-of-interest policy, committees — audit/finance/programs), per VS-36 governance standards
Foundation ED/Board pursue and maintain PCNC (Philippine Council for NGO Certification) accreditation — the standard NGO-credibility seal — with the documentary/financial evidence cycle
Audit/Finance ensure Foundation financial oversight (separate books, annual external audit, fund-use discipline) links to VS-21/VS-17, and report to the board

fields.Participants: Strategy (VS-33), Treasury (VS-18), Programs, Board Finance Committee
fields.Trigger: Annual budget (VS-33/VS-17.4); program approval; donation inflow
fields.Volume: CSR spend ~0.5–2% of net profit (PHP ~0.02B–0.1B/yr on a ~PHP 4–5B net-profit base) + endowment + donations

workflows.name: CSR Budgeting, Endowment & Fund Allocation Governance

Automation Opportunity: - Strategy-to-budget linkage; fund-use/destination tracking; spend-vs-impact dashboard
Controls: - CTL-686: CSR budget strategy-aligned; disbursement approval-matrix-governed; endowment policy-governed; board-reported (VS-36)
Cross-references: - links to VS-33/VS-17.4 (budget/FP&A), VS-18 (treasury/endowment), VS-36 (board), W4505 (strategy), W4514 (programs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Misallocation risk**: Spend not aligned to pillars/impact; mitigated by strategy-linked budget & approval matrix
- **Endowment-mismanagement risk**: Foundation assets mis-invested; mitigated by investment policy & board oversight
System Touchpoints: - Corporate budget/FP&A (VS-33/VS-17.4); treasury/endowment (VS-18); board governance (VS-36); GL (VS-17)
Time Estimate: - ~4 weeks annual budget; per-program approvals ongoing

steps.activity: Foundation ED/Finance build the annual CSR budget (corporate allocation + Foundation endowment draw + donations), aligned to the strategy pillars (W4505) and corporate budget (VS-33/VS-17.4)
Board Finance/Sustainability/ESG Manager allocate funds across programs/geographies with an approval matrix, governed disbursement, and fund-use restrictions (purpose-bounded per W4506)
steps.r: Board Finance / Sustainability/ESG Manager / Foundation ED

steps.activity: Finance/Treasury manage the endowment/investment policy (links to VS-18), track CSR spend vs budget, and report utilization to the board (VS-36)

fields.Volume: One CSR partnership-ethics standard across all partners/programs

workflows.name: CSR Policy, Code of Conduct & Partnership Ethics Standard

Automation Opportunity: - Partner-DD checklist/checks; sanction-list screening; political-use monitoring
Controls: - CTL-686 (ensure controlled execution — CSR Strategy, Governance & Foundation Operations (PA-152.1).)
- CTL-686: partners due-diligenced (VS-34/VS-86); no-political-use (VS-132); violations to speak-up (VS-119)
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-86 (ABC), VS-119 (ethics), VS-132 (political), VS-34/VS-03 (DD), VS-100.3 (legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Partner-fraud risk**: Funds to fraudulent/non-existent NGO; mitigated by due diligence & financial-integrity vetting
- **Political-misuse risk**: CSR funds used for political/election advantage (VS-132); mitigated by no-political-use rule & monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Compliance (VS-22); ABC (VS-86); ethics/speak-up (VS-119); political compliance (VS-132); procurement (VS-34); legal (VS-100.3)

steps.activity: Compliance/Foundation ED set the CSR partnership-ethics standard (partner due diligence, conflict-of-interest, anti-bribery in community dealings, no political-use) aligned to VS-86/VS-119/VS-132

Procurement/Programs apply partner due diligence (NGO/LGU/cooperative vetting, financial integrity, no terrorist/sanctioned-entity links) before funding, integrated to VS-34/VS-03 vendor due diligence

steps.a: VP Legal / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Compliance/Ethics monitor adherence, link violations to the speak-up channel (VS-119), and manage political-use risk (no CSR funds for election/political purpose VS-132)

fields.Participants: HR (VS-19/VS-103), Store Ops (VS-07), Volunteers, Shared Services (VS-72)
fields.Volume: Foundation staff + regional/field network across store communities

workflows.name: CSR Operating Model, Staffing & Field Network

Automation Opportunity: - Volunteer-management platform; field-network coordination app; shared-service chargeback (VS-72)
Controls: - CTL-686 (ensure controlled execution — CSR Strategy, Governance & Foundation Operations (PA-152.1).)
- CTL-686: operating model strategy-aligned; staff sustainably resourced; shared-services governed (VS-72)
Cross-references: - links to VS-121/VS-102/VS-19.4 (HR), VS-07 (store network), VS-72 (shared services), VS-103 (HRSS), W4505 (strategy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Understaffing risk**: Thin CSR team → programs under-delivered; mitigated by operating-model sizing & volunteer leverage
- **Burnout/turnover risk**: Field CSR roles demanding; mitigated by comp/dev (VS-102/VS-19.4) & sustainable load
System Touchpoints: - HR/recruit/comp (VS-121/VS-102/VS-19.4); store ops network (VS-07); shared services (VS-72); HRSS (VS-103)

steps.activity: Foundation ED/HR design the CSR operating model (central programs team + regional field coordinators + store-community liaisons leveraging store staff/network VS-07), per strategy (W4505)
HR/Foundation ED staff the team (recruit VS-121, compensate VS-102, develop VS-19.4), and define the volunteer/secondment model from the 6,762-employee base
Shared Services/Foundation ED provide shared back-office (finance/IT/HR) to the Foundation via VS-72 cross-entity services, and run the field-network coordination

Automation Opportunity: - Safeguarding incident case mgmt; fund-flow monitoring; risk-register integration (VS-21.2)
Controls: - CTL-686: CSR risks in ERM (VS-21.2); safeguarding/PSEA policy; violations to speak-up (VS-119); field-ops HSE (VS-24)
Cross-references: - links to VS-21.2 (ERM), VS-119 (speak-up), VS-24 (HSE), VS-21 (audit), VS-69 (disaster), W4508/W4509 (fund/DD)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Safeguarding-failure risk**: Beneficiary harm (esp. children/vulnerable) → severe reputational/legal exposure; mitigated by PSEA/child-safeguarding policy & speak-up linkage
- **Fund-misuse risk**: Misappropriated community funds; mitigated by DD (W4509), fund-use tracking (W4508), audit (VS-21)
System Touchpoints: - ERM/risk (VS-21.2); ethics/speak-up (VS-119); HSE (VS-24); audit (VS-21); legal (VS-100.3); disaster ops (VS-69)

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / Foundation Board
steps.activity: Risk/Foundation ED identify CSR/Foundation risks (fund misuse, beneficiary safeguarding/PSEA, partner fraud, reputational, disaster-ops safety VS-69) and integrate to ERM (VS-21.2)

steps.a: VP Legal / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Compliance/Foundation ED establish beneficiary safeguarding (protection from sexual exploitation & abuse, child-safeguarding for education programs) and link violations to speak-up (VS-119)

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / Foundation Board
steps.activity: Audit/HSE verify safeguarding/HSE in community/disaster field ops (links to VS-24/VS-69) and report to the board risk committee

Automation Opportunity: - Integrated grants/impact/volunteer platform; automated beneficiary de-identification; impact dashboards
Controls: - CTL-686 (ensure controlled execution — CSR Strategy, Governance & Foundation Operations (PA-152.1).)
- CTL-686: CSR systems EA-governed (VS-113); impact data unified; beneficiary data secured/privacy-respecting (VS-91/VS-27.3)
Cross-references: - links to VS-27/VS-28 (IT/data), VS-113 (EA), VS-17 (finance), VS-27.3/VS-91/VS-88 (security/privacy/retention), W4521 (impact)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-fragmentation risk**: Impact data scattered → unmeasurable outcomes; mitigated by unified data model
- **Beneficiary-privacy risk**: PII of vulnerable beneficiaries exposed; mitigated by security (VS-27.3) & privacy (VS-91)
System Touchpoints: - IT/data (VS-27/VS-28); EA (VS-113); finance/GL (VS-17); security (VS-27.3); privacy (VS-91); retention (VS-88)

steps.activity: IT/EA/Foundation ED design the CSR/Foundation systems landscape (grants/partnership mgmt, volunteer platform, beneficiary/impact data, donations), per EA standards (VS-113)
Data/Foundation ED build the impact-measurement data model (beneficiaries, outcomes, indicators) on the platform (VS-28), integrated to finance (W4508 fund-use) and partner data
Security/Privacy ensure beneficiary/donor data is secured (VS-27.3) and privacy-respecting (VS-91 — beneficiary PII), with retention (VS-88)
